title: feat: add per-user RPM limits for burst-heavy models
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- Sets registry `perUserRpm` limits: Flux/Z-Image/Klein 60; DreamShaper 300; DeepSeek/Qwen TTS 30; Seedream 5/Nemotron 20; MiniMax/Muse Glimmer/Mistral 10; Llama Scout 5.
- Uses the existing authenticated-user, canonical-model token bucket; aliases share the canonical limit and excess requests return the existing 429 response.
- Bases the added limits on production user-minute burst concentration, upstream 429s, and conservative traffic-impact estimates.
- Preserves providers, routes, pricing, access, capabilities, aliases, and fallbacks; the existing model catalog metadata displays each limit.
- Passes locked Biome formatting, the focused Worker rate-limit suite (4/4), and Gen typechecking.

gist.headline: The burst garden gets trellises
gist.blurb: A few especially popular model paths now have per-user pacing rails, so the whole garden gets a steadier share of sunlight. The model catalog also shows the limits before anyone discovers them the traditional way: a 429.
gist.summary: Added authenticated per-user RPM limits to burst-heavy canonical models—60 RPM for Flux, Z-Image, and Klein; 300 for DreamShaper; 30 for DeepSeek and Qwen TTS; plus model-specific 5–20 RPM caps—while aliases share each canonical token bucket.
gist.impact: Users can see each model's RPM limit in the catalog, and concentrated bursts now receive the existing 429 response while providers, pricing, routes, access, aliases, and fallbacks remain unchanged.
gist.visual_concept: Depict Polli tending a cozy garden of labeled model-plants, each growing through small wooden trellises that represent per-user RPM pacing. A friendly CRT robot reads a model catalog sign with tiny rate badges, while a gentle token-bucket fountain distributes water evenly among Flux, DreamShaper, TTS, and other plants.
